quick_ref.Grammar Focus: Simple sentence S+V+O, am / is / are (be verb)
quick_ref.Key Pattern: "My name is Max. I am a student."
quick_ref.Vocabulary: 8 Tier 1 words (name, age, boy, girl, student, happy, nice, friend)

methodology.title: 2.1 Core Principle: Foundation of Identity
content: Problem: Students at the beginning of the program lack the basic structures to introduce themselves confidently.

Solution: Week 1 establishes the absolute foundation. We focus on the "be" verb (am/is/are) and basic identity nouns/adjectives so students can construct simple, accurate sentences about who they are.

methodology.title: 2.2 Session Flow (120 Minutes)

vocab_tiers.Memory Trick: Definition: a drawing that shows information

parts.title: PART 1: READING INPUT  Title: "Hello World!"
content: Hello! My name (tên) is Max. I am a boy (con trai). I am eight years old.
This is Luna. She is a girl (con gái). Her age (tuổi) is nine.
Max and Luna are at school. They like to learn new things.
"I am a happy (vui vẻ) student," says Max.
"I am a good student," says Luna.
It is fun to meet new people!
T / F: Max is a boy.
T / F: Luna is eight years old.
Fill-in from text: I am a _________________ student, says Max.
[O] Stage 3B — Inference: Why is it fun to meet new people?

parts.title: PART 2: VOCABULARY BUILDING — Story Words: name, age, boy, girl + Cambridge Preview (Tier 2)
PART 3: SENTENCE BUILDING (DIVERSE EXERCISES)
content: Grammar Focus: Simple sentence S+V+O & "be" verb (am/is/are)
L1 — Match the sentence halves [ALL] (10 items)
My name is _________ a. a girl.
We are _________ f. nine years old.
The class is _________ j. very fun.
[O] L2 — Older: Unscramble the sentence (10 items)
Student B: "My name is Luna. I am a girl!"
[O] L3 — Older: Fill in the blank with 3 options (10 items)
She is a happy _______________. (girl / dog / tree)
I am eight _______________ old. (years / days / ages)
The class _______________ very fun. (is / are / am)
Base: My name is Max. + Add: (and I am happy)
Base: I am a student. + Add: (good)
Base: I am a boy. + Add: (eight years old)
Base: Luna is a girl. + Add: (smart)
Base: She is nine. + Add: (years old)
Base: The class is fun. + Add: (very)
Base: I like school. + Add: (my new)

parts.title: PART 4: LISTENING PRACTICE — Cambridge Flyers Listening format
content: ☐ The story is about driving a car. ☐ The story is about introducing names. ☐ The story is about flying an airplane.
C. Stage 3B — Inference: Why is it fun to meet new people?
D. Dictation (teacher reads twice — students write 1 sentence):

parts.title: PART 5: ERROR CORRECTION (Find the hidden mistake — story + grammar)
content: Type A: I is a happy boy.
Type B: My names are Max.
Type C: She am nine years old.

parts.title: PART 6: STEM/CLIL — Data Collection: Who are we?
content: Read this: Scientists collect data! Data is information. We can collect data about our classroom. How many boys are in the class? How many girls? We can count them and write the numbers down. This helps us know more about our friends. Counting is the first step in science!
The diagram shows: A chart showing 3 boys and 4 girls in a classroom.
🔍 YouTube for teacher: Search "Data collection for kids STEM"

parts.title: PART 1: READING INPUT  Title: "We Are Students!"
content: We are in the classroom. I am a student (học sinh).
Luna is a student, too. She is a smart girl (con gái).
We like to read books. We like to draw pictures.
"Are you happy (vui vẻ) today?" asks the teacher.
"Yes, we are very happy!" we say.
School is a great place to be a student!
T / F: They are in the park.
T / F: Luna is a smart girl.
Fill-in from text: Yes, we are very _________________! we say.
[O] Stage 3B — Inference: Why is school a great place?

parts.title: PART 2: VOCABULARY BUILDING — Deep review story words + Cambridge words (Tier 2 complete set)
PART 3: SENTENCE BUILDING (DIVERSE EXERCISES)
content: Grammar Focus: Simple sentence S+V+O (Continuing "be" verb)
L1 — Write Yes or No [ALL] (10 items)
"I am nine years old" is correct. _________
[O] L2 — Older: Unscramble the sentence (10 items)
Student B: "Yes, I am a student! I am happy!"
[O] L3 — Older: Fill in the blank with 3 options (10 items)
She is a smart _______________. (girl / tree / bird)
You _______________ a good friend. (are / is / am)
He _______________ an eight-year-old boy. (is / are / am)
_______________ is a fun place. (School / Sleep / Eat)
Base: I am a student. + Add: (good)
Base: She is a girl. + Add: (smart)
Base: He is a boy. + Add: (tall)
Base: Her name is Luna. + Add: (and she is nice)
Base: His name is Max. + Add: (and he is happy)
Base: I am nine. + Add: (years old)
Base: We are students. + Add: (in the classroom)

parts.title: PART 5: ERROR CORRECTION (Find the hidden mistake — story + grammar)
content: Type A: We is happy students.

parts.title: PART 6: STEM/CLIL — Data Collection: Our Feelings
content: Read this: We collected data about boys and girls. Now, let's collect data about feelings! Scientists ask questions to collect data. They ask, "Are you happy today?" If you say yes, they write it down. We can draw a chart showing happy students. Data helps us see the truth!
The diagram shows: A chart showing 5 happy faces and 1 sad face in a classroom.
🔍 YouTube for teacher: Search "Feelings data collection kids STEM"

parts.title: PART 1: READING INPUT  Title: "Nice Friends"
content: I have a friend (bạn bè) named Pip. Pip is a squirrel!
Pip is very nice (tốt bụng). He shares his food with me.
"You are a good friend," I tell Pip.
At school, all the students are nice. We help each other.
It is very important to be nice. Nice friends make us happy!
T / F: Pip is a dog.
T / F: Pip is very nice.
Fill-in from text: We are _________________ friends, says Pip.
[O] Stage 3B — Inference: Why is it important to be nice to your friends?

parts.title: PART 2: VOCABULARY BUILDING — Mastery Level: ALL 8 story words + ALL 3 Cambridge words
PART 3: SENTENCE BUILDING (DIVERSE EXERCISES)
content: Grammar Focus: Bringing it all together (S+V+O & Adjectives)
Review: I am... He is... We are...
Adding Adjectives: She is a nice friend. We are happy students.
Pip là một người bạn tốt bụng.
Bạn là một người bạn tốt.
Mọi học sinh đều tốt bụng.
Những người bạn tốt làm chúng tôi vui vẻ.
Tôi rất vui vì bạn là bạn của tôi.
Cô ấy giúp đỡ bạn bè của mình.
Anh ấy là một cậu bé tốt bụng.
Tên của người bạn của tôi là Luna.
Lớp học của chúng tôi thì tuyệt vời!
[O] L2 — Older: Unscramble the sentence (10 items)
glad / I / you / my / friend. / are / am
Student A: "Are you a nice friend?"
Student B: "Yes, I am a nice friend! I share my food!"
[O] L3 — Older: Fill in the blank with 3 options (10 items)
Pip is a _______________ friend. (nice / rock / car)
You _______________ a good boy. (are / is / am)
Nice friends make us _______________. (happy / sad / scary)
It is _______________ to be nice. (important / bad / sleepy)
Base: Pip is a friend. + Add: (nice)
Base: You are a friend. + Add: (good)
Base: The students are nice. + Add: (all)
Base: Friends make us happy. + Add: (Nice)
Base: She helps her friends. + Add: (always)
Base: He is a boy. + Add: (nice)
Base: My friend's name is Luna. + Add: (best)
Base: Our class is great! + Add: (very)
Base: I am a student. + Add: (happy)

parts.title: PART 6: STEM/CLIL — Data Collection: Our Friends
content: Read this: We can use data to understand our community! Scientists collect data to see how many friends we have. They can make a chart. Data shows that nice students have more friends. Collecting data about friends helps us build a happy classroom!
The diagram shows: A chart showing students sharing toys and making new friends.

games.name: Vocab Slam
games.session_fit: All formats — best after vocab intro (P3) in any session
games.materials: Vocab flashcards W1: name, age, boy, girl, student
instructions: Round 1: Teacher calls a Vietnamese meaning — first student to say the English word AND use it correctly in a sentence wins the card.
Round 2: Reverse — teacher calls English word, student gives Vietnamese + memory trick.
Bonus round: Students chain all vocab words (name, age, boy, girl, student) into one connected story using sequence connectors from this week.
Team variant: 2 teams, 10 cards per round. Team with highest score wins.

games.name: Grammar Relay
games.session_fit: Best in Drill slot (Slot 2) or after P4/P6 in 3-session mode
games.materials: 10 sentence cards — 5 correct, 5 with errors based on: Simple sentence S+V+O, am / is / are (be verb)
instructions: Grammar focus this week: Simple sentence S+V+O, am / is / are (be verb).
Speed Read: Display sentence for 5 sec. Teams write C (correct) or E (error) on whiteboards simultaneously — no copying allowed.
Fix-It: For error sentences, team that corrects fastest AND explains the rule earns double points.
Build: Each team member adds 1 original sentence using the grammar target. The chain must be logically connected — each sentence must link to the previous.

games.name: Story Race
games.session_fit: All formats — best in final slot of the week (S3 / Slot 5 / Session B)
games.materials: Story starter card: theme "Introductions & Identity — Hello World!"
instructions: Give each pair a story starter connected to this week's theme: "Introductions & Identity — Hello World!".
Pair A adds 2 sentences — must include at least 2 vocab words from this week.
Pass to Pair B: they MUST correct any grammar mistake from Pair A first, then add 2 more sentences using different vocab words.
Final round: Each pair presents their story ending aloud. Class votes on most creative + most accurate (name, age, boy, girl, student usage). Teacher scores grammar precision.

10.unit_theme: Community & Routines — The Hero Academy: Farm vs City

quick_ref.Theme: The Hero Academy — Farm vs City
quick_ref.Key Pattern: "The city is busy, but the farm is peaceful."
quick_ref.Vocabulary: 10 Tier 1 (Farm & Contrast words)

methodology.title: 2.1 Core Principle: The Power of Contrast
content: Problem: Students can describe a single place or object, but lack the connecting words to compare two different things in one fluid thought.

Solution: We introduce the conjunction "but" to show contrast. By comparing two distinctly different environments (Farm vs. City), students naturally practice pairing opposing adjectives (noisy/quiet, busy/peaceful) and connecting two independent clauses.

methodology.title: 2.2 Session Flow (120 Minutes)
content: Session 1: Introduce the farm setting and basic contrasts (city vs. farm, noisy vs. quiet).
Session 2: Focus on farm animals (cow, chicken, pig) and what exists in each place.
Session 3: Consolidate the environments (countryside, field, fresh air) and express personal preferences using "but".

methodology.title: 2.3 Vocabulary Tiering System

content: S1 pull-out: Ask the student: "Is the city quiet?" -> Student: "The city is noisy, but the farm is quiet."
S2 pull-out: Ask the student: "What animals are on the farm?" -> Student: "There are cows, chickens, and pigs."
Communicative task (Section 8): Information Gap. Students debate and compare two pictures (one of a city, one of a farm) to find differences.

Bonus round: Students chain all vocab words (farm, countryside, peaceful, clean, fresh) into one connected story using sequence connectors from this week.
Team variant: 2 teams, 10 cards per round. Team with highest score wins.

games.name: Grammar Relay
games.session_fit: Best in Drill slot (Slot 2) or after P4/P6 in 3-session mode
games.materials: 10 sentence cards — 5 correct, 5 with errors based on: "but" for contrast
instructions: Grammar focus this week: "but" for contrast.
Speed Read: Display sentence for 5 sec. Teams write C (correct) or E (error) on whiteboards simultaneously — no copying allowed.
Fix-It: For error sentences, team that corrects fastest AND explains the rule earns double points.
Build: Each team member adds 1 original sentence using the grammar target. The chain must be logically connected — each sentence must link to the previous.

games.name: Story Race
games.session_fit: All formats — best in final slot of the week (S3 / Slot 5 / Session B)
games.materials: Story starter card: theme "Community & Routines — The Hero Academy: Farm vs City"
instructions: Give each pair a story starter connected to this week's theme: "Community & Routines — The Hero Academy: Farm vs City".
Pair A adds 2 sentences — must include at least 2 vocab words from this week.
Pass to Pair B: they MUST correct any grammar mistake from Pair A first, then add 2 more sentences using different vocab words.
Final round: Each pair presents their story ending aloud. Class votes on most creative + most accurate (farm, countryside, peaceful, clean, fresh usage). Teacher scores grammar precision.

methodology.title: 2.1 Core Principle: Contextual Location Linking
content: Problem: Students often confuse prepositions of location (in, on, at).

Solution: This week introduces "at" specifically anchored to public places and weekend activities (at the park, at the library). By consistently pairing the action verb with the location noun, students naturally acquire the "verb + at the + place" chunk.

methodology.title: 2.2 Session Flow (120 Minutes)
2.3 Vocabulary Tiering System
2.4 Teacher Notes: Pull-Out Tasks & Communicative Task
content: S1 pull-out: Show a place flashcard (e.g., park). Student must make a full sentence: "I am at the park."
S2 pull-out: Show an action flashcard (e.g., read). Student matches it to a place: "I read at the library."
Communicative task: Information Gap (Section 8). Student A knows where Max goes. Student B knows where Luna goes. They ask and answer to complete the weekend schedules.

games.name: Vocab Slam
games.session_fit: All formats — best after vocab intro (P3) in any session
games.materials: Vocab flashcards W11: park, library, supermarket, cinema, restaurant
instructions: Round 1: Teacher calls a Vietnamese meaning — first student to say the English word AND use it correctly in a sentence wins the card.
Round 2: Reverse — teacher calls English word, student gives Vietnamese + memory trick.
Bonus round: Students chain all vocab words (park, library, supermarket, cinema, restaurant) into one connected story using sequence connectors from this week.
Team variant: 2 teams, 10 cards per round. Team with highest score wins.

games.name: Grammar Relay
games.session_fit: Best in Drill slot (Slot 2) or after P4/P6 in 3-session mode
games.materials: 10 sentence cards — 5 correct, 5 with errors based on: Preposition "at" for places
instructions: Grammar focus this week: Preposition "at" for places.
Speed Read: Display sentence for 5 sec. Teams write C (correct) or E (error) on whiteboards simultaneously — no copying allowed.
Fix-It: For error sentences, team that corrects fastest AND explains the rule earns double points.
Build: Each team member adds 1 original sentence using the grammar target. The chain must be logically connected — each sentence must link to the previous.

games.name: Story Race
games.session_fit: All formats — best in final slot of the week (S3 / Slot 5 / Session B)
games.materials: Story starter card: theme "Community & Routines — Weekend Adventures"
instructions: Give each pair a story starter connected to this week's theme: "Community & Routines — Weekend Adventures".
Pair A adds 2 sentences — must include at least 2 vocab words from this week.
Pass to Pair B: they MUST correct any grammar mistake from Pair A first, then add 2 more sentences using different vocab words.
Final round: Each pair presents their story ending aloud. Class votes on most creative + most accurate (park, library, supermarket, cinema, restaurant usage). Teacher scores grammar precision.

methodology.title: 2.1 Core Principle: Action & Ability Linking
content: Problem: Students often forget to drop the "to" after "can" (e.g., saying "I can to play").

Solution: This week anchors the modal "can" and "can't" directly to bare infinitive action verbs. By chanting and acting out the chunks ("can sing", "can't fly"), students internalize the pattern naturally. TPR (Total Physical Response) is heavily used to demonstrate abilities.

2.3 Vocabulary Tiering System
2.4 Teacher Notes: Pull-Out Tasks & Communicative Task
content: S1 pull-out: Show an action flashcard (e.g., sing). Student must make an affirmative sentence: "I can sing."
S2 pull-out: Show an action flashcard. Student must make a negative sentence: "I can't swim."
Communicative task: Information Gap (Section 8). Student A knows what Max can do. Student B knows what Luna can do. They ask and answer to fill the talent show roster.

"I can swim in the water," she says. "I swim very fast."
"I can climb a tall tree," she says.
"I can't fly in the sky," she says.
"And I can't ride a bike yet."
Max smiles at Luna. "That is okay!" he says.
"We can't do everything. But we can learn!"
Luna is happy. She climbs a tree for the talent show!
T / F: Luna can fly in the sky.
T / F: Luna can swim fast.
Fill-in from text: "We can't do _______________. But we can learn!"
[O] Stage 3B — Inference: Why is Luna happy at the end?

games.name: Vocab Slam
games.session_fit: All formats — best after vocab intro (P3) in any session
games.materials: Vocab flashcards W12: can, can't, sing, dance, run
instructions: Round 1: Teacher calls a Vietnamese meaning — first student to say the English word AND use it correctly in a sentence wins the card.
Round 2: Reverse — teacher calls English word, student gives Vietnamese + memory trick.
Bonus round: Students chain all vocab words (can, can't, sing, dance, run) into one connected story using sequence connectors from this week.
Team variant: 2 teams, 10 cards per round. Team with highest score wins.

games.name: Grammar Relay
games.session_fit: Best in Drill slot (Slot 2) or after P4/P6 in 3-session mode
games.materials: 10 sentence cards — 5 correct, 5 with errors based on: Can / Can't (Ability)
instructions: Grammar focus this week: Can / Can't (Ability).
Speed Read: Display sentence for 5 sec. Teams write C (correct) or E (error) on whiteboards simultaneously — no copying allowed.
Fix-It: For error sentences, team that corrects fastest AND explains the rule earns double points.
Build: Each team member adds 1 original sentence using the grammar target. The chain must be logically connected — each sentence must link to the previous.

games.name: Story Race
games.session_fit: All formats — best in final slot of the week (S3 / Slot 5 / Session B)
games.materials: Story starter card: theme "Community & Routines — The Talent Show"
instructions: Give each pair a story starter connected to this week's theme: "Community & Routines — The Talent Show".
Pair A adds 2 sentences — must include at least 2 vocab words from this week.
Pass to Pair B: they MUST correct any grammar mistake from Pair A first, then add 2 more sentences using different vocab words.
Final round: Each pair presents their story ending aloud. Class votes on most creative + most accurate (can, can't, sing, dance, run usage). Teacher scores grammar precision.

methodology.title: 2.1 Core Principle: The "S" Snake (Third Person Singular)
content: Problem: Students often forget to add 's' or 'es' when talking about He/She/It in the present simple.

Solution: We introduce the concept of the "S" Snake. When we talk about "I" or "You", the verb is normal. But when we point to a friend ("He" or "She"), the "S" Snake attaches to the action word (wake → wakes, go → goes). TPR (Total Physical Response) is used to physically mimic adding an 's' to the end of the action.

games.name: Vocab Slam
games.session_fit: All formats — best after vocab intro (P3) in any session
games.materials: Vocab flashcards W13: wake up, brush teeth, eat breakfast, go to school, study
instructions: Round 1: Teacher calls a Vietnamese meaning — first student to say the English word AND use it correctly in a sentence wins the card.
Round 2: Reverse — teacher calls English word, student gives Vietnamese + memory trick.
Bonus round: Students chain all vocab words (wake up, brush teeth, eat breakfast, go to school, study) into one connected story using sequence connectors from this week.
Team variant: 2 teams, 10 cards per round. Team with highest score wins.

games.name: Grammar Relay
games.session_fit: Best in Drill slot (Slot 2) or after P4/P6 in 3-session mode
games.materials: 10 sentence cards — 5 correct, 5 with errors based on: Present Simple (I verb / He verbs)
instructions: Grammar focus this week: Present Simple (I verb / He verbs).
Speed Read: Display sentence for 5 sec. Teams write C (correct) or E (error) on whiteboards simultaneously — no copying allowed.
Fix-It: For error sentences, team that corrects fastest AND explains the rule earns double points.
Build: Each team member adds 1 original sentence using the grammar target. The chain must be logically connected — each sentence must link to the previous.

games.name: Story Race
games.session_fit: All formats — best in final slot of the week (S3 / Slot 5 / Session B)
games.materials: Story starter card: theme "Community & Routines — A Day in Hero Life"
instructions: Give each pair a story starter connected to this week's theme: "Community & Routines — A Day in Hero Life".
Pair A adds 2 sentences — must include at least 2 vocab words from this week.
Pass to Pair B: they MUST correct any grammar mistake from Pair A first, then add 2 more sentences using different vocab words.

Final round: Each pair presents their story ending aloud. Class votes on most creative + most accurate (wake up, brush teeth, eat breakfast, go to school, study usage). Teacher scores grammar precision.

methodology.title: 2.1 Core Principle: Project-Based Synthesis
content: Problem: Students learn grammar rules in isolation but struggle to combine them into a cohesive paragraph about themselves.

Solution: Week 14 acts as a capstone for Block A. There is no "new" grammar. Instead, students synthesize what they know to build a "Welcome to My World" poster. Session 1 focuses on drafting Identity & Family. Session 2 focuses on Abilities & Routines. Session 3 focuses on the final Presentation Delivery.

methodology.title: 2.2 Session Flow (120 Minutes)
2.3 Vocabulary Tiering System
2.4 Teacher Notes: Pull-Out Tasks & Communicative Task
content: S1 pull-out: Bring students to the drafting table. Ask: "Who is in your family?" Student writes 1 sentence for their poster.
S2 pull-out: Ask: "What can you do?" and "What time do you wake up?". Student writes 2 sentences for their poster.
Communicative task: Information Gap (Section 8). Students practice asking presentation questions to their peers to prepare for the final Showcase.

games.name: Vocab Slam
games.session_fit: All formats — best after vocab intro (P3) in any session
games.materials: Vocab flashcards W14: hero, family, happy, city, building
instructions: Round 1: Teacher calls a Vietnamese meaning — first student to say the English word AND use it correctly in a sentence wins the card.
Round 2: Reverse — teacher calls English word, student gives Vietnamese + memory trick.
Bonus round: Students chain all vocab words (hero, family, happy, city, building) into one connected story using sequence connectors from this week.
Team variant: 2 teams, 10 cards per round. Team with highest score wins.

games.name: Grammar Relay
games.session_fit: Best in Drill slot (Slot 2) or after P4/P6 in 3-session mode
games.materials: 10 sentence cards — 5 correct, 5 with errors based on: Review: To be, Have, There is/are, Can, Present Simple
instructions: Grammar focus this week: Review: To be, Have, There is/are, Can, Present Simple.
Speed Read: Display sentence for 5 sec. Teams write C (correct) or E (error) on whiteboards simultaneously — no copying allowed.
Fix-It: For error sentences, team that corrects fastest AND explains the rule earns double points.
Build: Each team member adds 1 original sentence using the grammar target. The chain must be logically connected — each sentence must link to the previous.

games.name: Story Race
games.session_fit: All formats — best in final slot of the week (S3 / Slot 5 / Session B)
games.materials: Story starter card: theme "Community & Routines — Hero Showcase Day"
instructions: Give each pair a story starter connected to this week's theme: "Community & Routines — Hero Showcase Day".

Pass to Pair B: they MUST correct any grammar mistake from Pair A first, then add 2 more sentences using different vocab words.

methodology.title: 2.1 Core Principle: The "Right Now" Camera
content: Problem: Students often confuse Present Simple (routines) with Present Continuous (actions happening right now), forgetting the "to be" verb or the "-ing" tail.

Solution: We introduce the "Live Camera" concept. When the camera is recording right now, the action gets an "-ing" tail, and it always needs a helper (am/is/are) holding the camera. Students act as "Live Reporters" describing exactly what they see at this very moment. TPR emphasizes the ongoing nature of the action (e.g., continuously moving arms while saying "runn-ing").

methodology.title: 2.2 Session Flow (120 Minutes)
2.3 Vocabulary Tiering System
2.4 Teacher Notes: Pull-Out Tasks & Communicative Task
content: S1 pull-out: Show an action flashcard (e.g., running). Student makes a "He/She is..." sentence: "He is running."
S2 pull-out: Show a flashcard with multiple people. Student makes a "They are..." sentence: "They are talking."
Communicative task: Information Gap (Section 8). Student A has a picture of half the park, Student B has the other half. They ask "What is he doing?" to fill in their scene.

games.name: Vocab Slam
games.session_fit: All formats — best after vocab intro (P3) in any session
games.materials: Vocab flashcards W15: running, walking, sitting, eating, playing
instructions: Round 1: Teacher calls a Vietnamese meaning — first student to say the English word AND use it correctly in a sentence wins the card.
Round 2: Reverse — teacher calls English word, student gives Vietnamese + memory trick.
Bonus round: Students chain all vocab words (running, walking, sitting, eating, playing) into one connected story using sequence connectors from this week.
Team variant: 2 teams, 10 cards per round. Team with highest score wins.

games.name: Grammar Relay
games.session_fit: Best in Drill slot (Slot 2) or after P4/P6 in 3-session mode
games.materials: 10 sentence cards — 5 correct, 5 with errors based on: Present Continuous: am/is/are + V-ing
instructions: Grammar focus this week: Present Continuous: am/is/are + V-ing.
Speed Read: Display sentence for 5 sec. Teams write C (correct) or E (error) on whiteboards simultaneously — no copying allowed.
Fix-It: For error sentences, team that corrects fastest AND explains the rule earns double points.
Build: Each team member adds 1 original sentence using the grammar target. The chain must be logically connected — each sentence must link to the previous.

games.name: Story Race
games.session_fit: All formats — best in final slot of the week (S3 / Slot 5 / Session B)
games.materials: Story starter card: theme "Community & Routines — The Busy Park (Actions Now)"
instructions: Give each pair a story starter connected to this week's theme: "Community & Routines — The Busy Park (Actions Now)".
Pair A adds 2 sentences — must include at least 2 vocab words from this week.
Pass to Pair B: they MUST correct any grammar mistake from Pair A first, then add 2 more sentences using different vocab words.
Final round: Each pair presents their story ending aloud. Class votes on most creative + most accurate (running, walking, sitting, eating, playing usage). Teacher scores grammar precision.

teacher_contents.in_class_speaking:
IN-CLASS SPEAKING ACTIVITIES — Session 1 (teacher-led)

Activity 1 — Pair Speaking (3–5 min, pairs):
  Student A: Act out an action (e.g., eating).
  Student B: Describe it ("You are eating!"). Switch.

Challenge Extension (L3 — for advanced/older students):
  [O] L3 — Older: Fill in the blank with 3 options (10 items)
  He _______________ (is / am / are) running fast.
  She is _______________ (walking / walk / walks) her dog.
  The woman is _______________ (sitting / sit / sits) on a bench.

methodology.title: 2.1 Core Principle: The Live Sports Commentator
content: Problem: Students often forget the spelling rules for adding "-ing" (e.g., doubling consonants in running, dropping 'e' in scoring) and struggle to speak continuously.

Solution: We turn the classroom into a "Live Sports Channel". Students act as sports commentators. Because sports happen in real-time, the Present Continuous (am/is/are + V-ing) is the only natural tense to use. TPR involves mimicking the sports actions (kicking an imaginary ball, cheering for a win) while emphasizing the "-ing" spelling rules during writing tasks.

content: S1 pull-out: Toss a soft ball to a student. Ask: "What are you doing?" Student: "I am catching the ball."
S2 pull-out: Show a scoreboard where Team A has 10 points and Team B has 2. Ask: "Who is winning?" Student: "Team A is winning. Team B is losing."
Communicative task: Information Gap (Section 8). Student A has half the sports scene. Student B has the other. They ask "What is Max doing?" to complete the live report.

games.name: Vocab Slam
games.session_fit: All formats — best after vocab intro (P3) in any session
games.materials: Vocab flashcards W16: kick, throw, catch, hit, score
instructions: Round 1: Teacher calls a Vietnamese meaning — first student to say the English word AND use it correctly in a sentence wins the card.
Round 2: Reverse — teacher calls English word, student gives Vietnamese + memory trick.
Bonus round: Students chain all vocab words (kick, throw, catch, hit, score) into one connected story using sequence connectors from this week.
Team variant: 2 teams, 10 cards per round. Team with highest score wins.

games.name: Grammar Relay
games.session_fit: Best in Drill slot (Slot 2) or after P4/P6 in 3-session mode
games.materials: 10 sentence cards — 5 correct, 5 with errors based on: Present Continuous with sports verbs
instructions: Grammar focus this week: Present Continuous with sports verbs.
Speed Read: Display sentence for 5 sec. Teams write C (correct) or E (error) on whiteboards simultaneously — no copying allowed.
Fix-It: For error sentences, team that corrects fastest AND explains the rule earns double points.
Build: Each team member adds 1 original sentence using the grammar target. The chain must be logically connected — each sentence must link to the previous.

games.name: Story Race
games.session_fit: All formats — best in final slot of the week (S3 / Slot 5 / Session B)
games.materials: Story starter card: theme "Community & Routines — Sports Commentary"
instructions: Give each pair a story starter connected to this week's theme: "Community & Routines — Sports Commentary".
Pair A adds 2 sentences — must include at least 2 vocab words from this week.
Pass to Pair B: they MUST correct any grammar mistake from Pair A first, then add 2 more sentences using different vocab words.
Final round: Each pair presents their story ending aloud. Class votes on most creative + most accurate (kick, throw, catch, hit, score usage). Teacher scores grammar precision.

17.unit_theme: The World Around Us — Weather Mission

quick_ref.Key Pattern: "It is [raining], so I am wearing a [coat]."
quick_ref.Vocabulary: 10 Tier 1 (production)

methodology.title: 2.1 Core Principle: Cause and Effect Linking
content: Problem: Students know weather words and clothing words, but struggle to connect them logically using conjunctions like "so".

Solution: This week introduces the logical bridge "so" (vì vậy) to connect a weather condition (Cause) with a clothing choice (Effect). We combine the Present Continuous for weather ("It is raining") with the Present Continuous for personal state ("I am wearing"). TPR involves looking up at the "sky", declaring the weather, and physically acting out putting on the corresponding clothing item.

methodology.title: 2.2 Session Flow (120 Minutes)
2.3 Vocabulary Tiering System
2.4 Teacher Notes: Pull-Out Tasks & Communicative Task
content: S1 pull-out: Show a "rain" card. Student says: "It is raining, so I am holding an umbrella."
S2 pull-out: Show a "windy" card. Student says: "It is windy, so I am wearing a hat."
Communicative task: Information Gap (Section 8). Student A has the weather. Student B has the clothes. They must match them using "so".

parts.title: PART 1: READING INPUT  Max's Weather Mission
content: Max is going on a mission today.
He looks at the sky. It is not sunny. The sky is dark.
"Oh no, it is raining!" says Max. "The water is falling."
"It is raining, so I am holding an umbrella," he says.
"It is cold, so I am wearing a thick coat."
Max is ready. He walks in the rain.
"Tomorrow, it is snowing," Max thinks. "I love the snow!"
T / F: The sky is very sunny today.
T / F: Max is wearing a thick coat.
What is falling from the dark sky?
Fill-in from text: "It is _______________, so I am holding an umbrella."
[O] Stage 3B — Inference: Why does Max need an umbrella and a coat?

parts.title: PART 2: VOCABULARY BUILDING — Story Words: raining, snowing, sunny, cloudy
content: → Memory trick: R-A-I-N: Rain Always Is Noisy
a. Look outside, it is _______________ (raining / book).
b. The sky is dark and it is _______________ (raining / happy).
→ Memory trick: S-N-O-W: Snow Never Opens Warm
a. It is _______________ (snowing / hot) and very cold.
b. I like it when it is _______________ (snowing / reading).
→ Memory trick: S-U-N: Sun Up Now
a. The sky is blue and it is _______________ (sunny / wet).
b. We play when it is _______________ (sunny / sleeping).
→ Memory trick: C-O-A-T: Cold Outside Always Take
a. I am wearing a thick _______________ (coat / sky).
b. The warm _______________ (coat / rain) is red.
→ Memory trick: U-M-B: Up My Body
a. I am holding a big _______________ (umbrella / dog).
b. The _______________ (umbrella / sun) keeps me dry.

content: Type A (missing 'to be'): It raining today. →

games.name: Vocab Slam
games.session_fit: All formats — best after vocab intro (P3) in any session
games.materials: Vocab flashcards W17: raining, snowing, sunny, cloudy, windy
instructions: Round 1: Teacher calls a Vietnamese meaning — first student to say the English word AND use it correctly in a sentence wins the card.
Round 2: Reverse — teacher calls English word, student gives Vietnamese + memory trick.
Bonus round: Students chain all vocab words (raining, snowing, sunny, cloudy, windy) into one connected story using sequence connectors from this week.
Team variant: 2 teams, 10 cards per round. Team with highest score wins.

games.name: Grammar Relay
games.session_fit: Best in Drill slot (Slot 2) or after P4/P6 in 3-session mode
games.materials: 10 sentence cards — 5 correct, 5 with errors based on: "It is V-ing" + "so" + "I am wearing..." (Cause/Effect)
instructions: Grammar focus this week: "It is V-ing" + "so" + "I am wearing..." (Cause/Effect).
Speed Read: Display sentence for 5 sec. Teams write C (correct) or E (error) on whiteboards simultaneously — no copying allowed.
Fix-It: For error sentences, team that corrects fastest AND explains the rule earns double points.
Build: Each team member adds 1 original sentence using the grammar target. The chain must be logically connected — each sentence must link to the previous.

games.name: Story Race
games.session_fit: All formats — best in final slot of the week (S3 / Slot 5 / Session B)
games.materials: Story starter card: theme "The World Around Us — Weather Mission"
instructions: Give each pair a story starter connected to this week's theme: "The World Around Us — Weather Mission".
Pair A adds 2 sentences — must include at least 2 vocab words from this week.
Pass to Pair B: they MUST correct any grammar mistake from Pair A first, then add 2 more sentences using different vocab words.
Final round: Each pair presents their story ending aloud. Class votes on most creative + most accurate (raining, snowing, sunny, cloudy, windy usage). Teacher scores grammar precision.

quick_ref.Theme: The Hero Academy — Hero Certification Test
quick_ref.Grammar Focus: Block A Review (To be, Have, Present Simple, Continuous, Can)

methodology.title: 2.1 Core Principle: Cumulative Retrieval & Assessment
content: Problem: Students memorize grammar for a specific week but fail to switch between tenses (e.g., Present Simple vs. Present Continuous) when required in a mixed context.

Solution: Week 18 is the "Hero Certification Test". Sessions 1 and 2 serve as high-intensity, mixed-skill reviews (Identity + Routines, then Abilities + Weather/Actions Now). Session 3 is a comprehensive checkpoint. We use a testing framework but maintain the supportive L1-L5 scaffolding. TPR shifts from teaching to "demonstration of mastery".

methodology.title: 2.2 Session Flow (120 Minutes)
2.3 Vocabulary Tiering System
2.4 Teacher Notes: Pull-Out Tasks & Communicative Task
content: S1 pull-out: Review Tense. Show a routine card -> "I wake up." Show an action card -> "I am running."
S2 pull-out: Review Connectors. Ask student to combine: "It is raining" + "I wear a coat" -> "It is raining, so I am wearing a coat."
Communicative task: Information Gap (Section 8). "Hero Examiner" interviews the "Hero Student" to test their English abilities.

parts.title: PART 1: READING INPUT  Max's Review Day
content: Today is the review day for the Hero Certification Test!
Max is studying very hard. He reviews his words.
"I am a brave hero," Max says. "I live in a modern city."
He looks at a picture of his mother.
"My mother is a good doctor. She works at a big hospital."
Then, Max writes about his routine.
"I wake up early in the morning every day. I brush my teeth."
Max knows how to talk about himself and his family.
He is ready for the first part of the test!
T / F: Max is a brave doctor.
T / F: Max lives in a modern city.
Fill-in from text: "I wake up early in the _______________ every day."
[O] Stage 3B — Inference: Why is Max studying hard today?

19.unit_theme: The Time Detective Agency — The Baby Photo Mystery

quick_ref.Theme: Time Detective Agency — The Baby Photo Mystery
quick_ref.Grammar Focus: was / were (Past state - NO action verbs)
quick_ref.Vocabulary: 10 Tier 1 (production)
quick_ref.VC Word Targets: S1=75w (20% blank) | S2=85w (25% blank) | S3=95w (30% blank)

methodology.title: 2.1 Core Principle: Time Machine Contrast (Now vs. Then)
content: Problem: Students often use "am/is/are" when talking about the past because they haven't established a clear mental timeline.

Solution: We introduce the "Time Machine". Everything in Block B happens in the past. We explicitly contrast the present state (Now) with the past state (Then) using visual cues like baby photos vs. current photos. The focus is purely on state (adjectives and nouns) using "was/were", completely avoiding action verbs so students master the copula verb in the past tense first.

methodology.title: 2.2 Session Flow (120 Minutes)
2.3 Vocabulary Tiering System
2.4 Teacher Notes: Pull-Out Tasks & Communicative Task
content: S1 pull-out: Show a baby photo. Ask: "Were you big?" Student answers: "No, I was small."
S2 pull-out: Contrast Now and Then. Teacher: "Now I am tall." Student responds with the past: "Then, I was little."
Communicative task: Information Gap (Section 8). "Time Detectives" look at clues (adjectives) to figure out who the baby in the mystery photo is.

games.name: Vocab Slam
games.session_fit: All formats — best after vocab intro (P3) in any session
games.materials: Vocab flashcards W19: baby, small, cute, little, noisy
instructions: Round 1: Teacher calls a Vietnamese meaning — first student to say the English word AND use it correctly in a sentence wins the card.
Round 2: Reverse — teacher calls English word, student gives Vietnamese + memory trick.
Bonus round: Students chain all vocab words (baby, small, cute, little, noisy) into one connected story using sequence connectors from this week.
Team variant: 2 teams, 10 cards per round. Team with highest score wins.

games.name: Grammar Relay
games.session_fit: Best in Drill slot (Slot 2) or after P4/P6 in 3-session mode
games.materials: 10 sentence cards — 5 correct, 5 with errors based on: was / were (Past state - NO action verbs)
instructions: Grammar focus this week: was / were (Past state - NO action verbs).
Speed Read: Display sentence for 5 sec. Teams write C (correct) or E (error) on whiteboards simultaneously — no copying allowed.
Fix-It: For error sentences, team that corrects fastest AND explains the rule earns double points.
Build: Each team member adds 1 original sentence using the grammar target. The chain must be logically connected — each sentence must link to the previous.

games.name: Story Race
games.session_fit: All formats — best in final slot of the week (S3 / Slot 5 / Session B)
games.materials: Story starter card: theme "The Time Detective Agency — The Baby Photo Mystery"
instructions: Give each pair a story starter connected to this week's theme: "The Time Detective Agency — The Baby Photo Mystery".
Pair A adds 2 sentences — must include at least 2 vocab words from this week.
Pass to Pair B: they MUST correct any grammar mistake from Pair A first, then add 2 more sentences using different vocab words.
Final round: Each pair presents their story ending aloud. Class votes on most creative + most accurate (baby, small, cute, little, noisy usage). Teacher scores grammar precision.

methodology.title: 2.1 Core Principle: The "Possession Pointer" (Đại từ sở hữu & Chỉ định)
content: Problem: Học sinh thường bối rối giữa các đại từ nhân xưng (I, He, She) và tính từ sở hữu (My, His, Her), hoặc quên dùng "This is" khi giới thiệu một người mới.

Solution: Sử dụng phương pháp "Possession Pointer" (Ngón tay sở hữu). Khi nói "This is", học sinh đưa tay ra phía trước như đang giới thiệu một người bạn. Khi nói "my", học sinh thu tay về chạm vào ngực mình để thể hiện sự sở hữu. Việc kết hợp hành động cơ thể (TPR) giúp não bộ ghi nhớ cấu trúc "This is my..." một cách trực quan và tự nhiên nhất.

methodology.title: 2.2 Session Flow (120 Minutes)
2.3 Vocabulary Tiering System
2.4 Teacher Notes: Pull-Out Tasks & Communicative Task
content: S1 pull-out: Đưa một bức ảnh gia đình (father). Yêu cầu học sinh giới thiệu: "This is my father."
S2 pull-out: Hỏi: "Is your brother tall or short?" Học sinh đáp: "My brother is tall."
Communicative task: Information Gap (Section 8). Học sinh A và B sẽ có hai bức ảnh gia đình khác nhau. Các em phải hỏi đáp để tìm ra đặc điểm của từng người trong gia đình đối phương.

games.name: Vocab Slam
games.session_fit: All formats — best after vocab intro (P3) in any session
games.materials: Vocab flashcards W2: family, team, mother, father, love
instructions: Round 1: Teacher calls a Vietnamese meaning — first student to say the English word AND use it correctly in a sentence wins the card.
Round 2: Reverse — teacher calls English word, student gives Vietnamese + memory trick.
Bonus round: Students chain all vocab words (family, team, mother, father, love) into one connected story using sequence connectors from this week.

methodology.title: 2.1 Core Principle: The "Time Binoculars" (Existence in Past)
content: Problem: Students confuse "It was" (describing a thing) with "There was" (stating that a thing existed in a place). They also forget to use "were" for plural nouns.

Solution: We introduce the "Time Binoculars". When we look at a place now, we say "There is/are". When we put on our Time Binoculars to look at an old picture, we must say "There was" (for one thing) or "There were" (for many things). We practice contrasting two pictures: "Now there are tall buildings. Then there were old trees." TPR involves putting hands like binoculars over the eyes when using the past tense.

2.3 Vocabulary Tiering System
2.4 Teacher Notes: Pull-Out Tasks & Communicative Task
content: S1 pull-out: Show a picture of one old house. Ask: "What was there?" Student: "There was an old building."

games.name: Vocab Slam
games.session_fit: All formats — best after vocab intro (P3) in any session
games.materials: Vocab flashcards W20: old, new, building, tree, river
instructions: Round 1: Teacher calls a Vietnamese meaning — first student to say the English word AND use it correctly in a sentence wins the card.
Round 2: Reverse — teacher calls English word, student gives Vietnamese + memory trick.
Bonus round: Students chain all vocab words (old, new, building, tree, river) into one connected story using sequence connectors from this week.
Team variant: 2 teams, 10 cards per round. Team with highest score wins.

games.name: Grammar Relay
games.session_fit: Best in Drill slot (Slot 2) or after P4/P6 in 3-session mode
games.materials: 10 sentence cards — 5 correct, 5 with errors based on: There was / There were (Past existence)
instructions: Grammar focus this week: There was / There were (Past existence).
Speed Read: Display sentence for 5 sec. Teams write C (correct) or E (error) on whiteboards simultaneously — no copying allowed.
Fix-It: For error sentences, team that corrects fastest AND explains the rule earns double points.
Build: Each team member adds 1 original sentence using the grammar target. The chain must be logically connected — each sentence must link to the previous.

games.name: Story Race
games.session_fit: All formats — best in final slot of the week (S3 / Slot 5 / Session B)
games.materials: Story starter card: theme "The Time Detective Agency — The Old Town Mystery"
instructions: Give each pair a story starter connected to this week's theme: "The Time Detective Agency — The Old Town Mystery".
Pair A adds 2 sentences — must include at least 2 vocab words from this week.
Pass to Pair B: they MUST correct any grammar mistake from Pair A first, then add 2 more sentences using different vocab words.
Final round: Each pair presents their story ending aloud. Class votes on most creative + most accurate (old, new, building, tree, river usage). Teacher scores grammar precision.

methodology.title: 2.1 Core Principle: The "Time Tail" (-ed)
content: Problem: Học sinh thường quên chia động từ ở quá khứ hoặc nhầm lẫn với thì hiện tại tiếp diễn (-ing).

Solution: Giới thiệu khái niệm "Cái đuôi thời gian" (The Time Tail). Khi một hành động đã hoàn thành vào ngày hôm qua (Yesterday), chúng ta phải gắn cái đuôi "-ed" vào sau động từ hành động. Giáo viên sử dụng TPR: khi nói động từ nguyên mẫu (walk), bước đi bình thường. Khi nói "walked", chỉ tay về phía sau lưng (tượng trưng cho quá khứ) để nhấn mạnh sự đã qua.

methodology.title: 2.2 Session Flow (120 Minutes)
2.3 Vocabulary Tiering System
2.4 Teacher Notes: Pull-Out Tasks & Communicative Task
content: S1 pull-out: Đưa một thẻ flashcard có hành động (vd: play). Học sinh thêm "-ed" và tạo câu: "Yesterday, I played."
S2 pull-out: Hỏi: "What did you do yesterday?" Học sinh dùng một động từ đã học để trả lời: "I cleaned my room."
Communicative task: Information Gap (Section 8). Học sinh đóng vai các Thám tử Thời gian kiểm tra "bằng chứng" (nhật ký) để tìm xem ai đã làm gì vào ngày hôm qua.

games.name: Vocab Slam
games.session_fit: All formats — best after vocab intro (P3) in any session
games.materials: Vocab flashcards W21: walked, looked, cooked, played, watched
instructions: Round 1: Teacher calls a Vietnamese meaning — first student to say the English word AND use it correctly in a sentence wins the card.
Round 2: Reverse — teacher calls English word, student gives Vietnamese + memory trick.
Bonus round: Students chain all vocab words (walked, looked, cooked, played, watched) into one connected story using sequence connectors from this week.
Team variant: 2 teams, 10 cards per round. Team with highest score wins.

games.name: Grammar Relay
games.session_fit: Best in Drill slot (Slot 2) or after P4/P6 in 3-session mode
games.materials: 10 sentence cards — 5 correct, 5 with errors based on: Past Simple Regular Verbs (-ed)
instructions: Grammar focus this week: Past Simple Regular Verbs (-ed).
Speed Read: Display sentence for 5 sec. Teams write C (correct) or E (error) on whiteboards simultaneously — no copying allowed.
Fix-It: For error sentences, team that corrects fastest AND explains the rule earns double points.
Build: Each team member adds 1 original sentence using the grammar target. The chain must be logically connected — each sentence must link to the previous.

games.name: Story Race
games.session_fit: All formats — best in final slot of the week (S3 / Slot 5 / Session B)
games.materials: Story starter card: theme "The Time Detective Agency — The Diary Evidence"
instructions: Give each pair a story starter connected to this week's theme: "The Time Detective Agency — The Diary Evidence".
Pair A adds 2 sentences — must include at least 2 vocab words from this week.
Pass to Pair B: they MUST correct any grammar mistake from Pair A first, then add 2 more sentences using different vocab words.
Final round: Each pair presents their story ending aloud. Class votes on most creative + most accurate (walked, looked, cooked, played, watched usage). Teacher scores grammar precision.

methodology.title: 2.1 Core Principle: The "Did" Thief (Kẻ trộm "Did")
content: Problem: Học sinh thường mắc lỗi chia thì quá khứ hai lần trong câu hỏi (ví dụ: Did you played? thay vì Did you play?).

Solution: Giới thiệu khái niệm "The Did Thief" (Kẻ trộm Did). Khi từ "Did" xuất hiện ở đầu câu hỏi, nó đã "ăn cắp" đuôi "-ed" của động từ chính. Do đó, động từ chính trở về dạng nguyên thể sạch sẽ (bare infinitive). Giáo viên dùng TPR: đưa tay ra trước làm động tác "tóm lấy" đuôi -ed khi nói "Did", và nhấn mạnh động từ nguyên thể phía sau.

methodology.title: 2.2 Session Flow (120 Minutes)
2.3 Vocabulary Tiering System
2.4 Teacher Notes: Pull-Out Tasks & Communicative Task
content: S1 pull-out: Đưa một thẻ hành động. Hỏi học sinh: "Did you [play] yesterday?" Học sinh trả lời: "Yes, I did." hoặc "No, I didn't."
S2 pull-out: Học sinh đóng vai thám tử, hỏi giáo viên một câu hỏi dùng "last night".
Communicative task: Information Gap (Section 8). "Interrogation Room" - Học sinh A là thám tử thẩm vấn Học sinh B (kẻ tình nghi) về các hoạt động trong quá khứ để tìm manh mối.

games.name: Vocab Slam
games.session_fit: All formats — best after vocab intro (P3) in any session
games.materials: Vocab flashcards W22: yesterday, last night, last week, last weekend, last month
instructions: Round 1: Teacher calls a Vietnamese meaning — first student to say the English word AND use it correctly in a sentence wins the card.
Round 2: Reverse — teacher calls English word, student gives Vietnamese + memory trick.
Bonus round: Students chain all vocab words (yesterday, last night, last week, last weekend, last month) into one connected story using sequence connectors from this week.
Team variant: 2 teams, 10 cards per round. Team with highest score wins.

games.name: Grammar Relay
games.session_fit: Best in Drill slot (Slot 2) or after P4/P6 in 3-session mode
games.materials: 10 sentence cards — 5 correct, 5 with errors based on: Did you...? Yes, I did. / No, I didn't.
instructions: Grammar focus this week: Did you...? Yes, I did. / No, I didn't..
Speed Read: Display sentence for 5 sec. Teams write C (correct) or E (error) on whiteboards simultaneously — no copying allowed.
Fix-It: For error sentences, team that corrects fastest AND explains the rule earns double points.
Build: Each team member adds 1 original sentence using the grammar target. The chain must be logically connected — each sentence must link to the previous.

games.name: Story Race
games.session_fit: All formats — best in final slot of the week (S3 / Slot 5 / Session B)
games.materials: Story starter card: theme "The Time Detective Agency — Interrogation Room"
instructions: Give each pair a story starter connected to this week's theme: "The Time Detective Agency — Interrogation Room".
Pair A adds 2 sentences — must include at least 2 vocab words from this week.
Pass to Pair B: they MUST correct any grammar mistake from Pair A first, then add 2 more sentences using different vocab words.

Final round: Each pair presents their story ending aloud. Class votes on most creative + most accurate (yesterday, last night, last week, last weekend, last month usage). Teacher scores grammar precision.

teacher_contents.stem_extension:
STEM/CLIL Extension Notes (teacher only):

PART 6: STEM/CLIL CONNECTION [ALL]
Measuring Time (Đo lường Thời gian)
The diagram shows: We use different tools to measure time in the past. For hours, like "this morning", we use a clock. For days and months, like "yesterday" or "last month", we use a calendar. Detectives must look at the clock and the calendar to solve mysteries!
What do we use to measure "this morning"? _______________ (a clock / an apple)
What do we use to measure "last month"? _______________ (a calendar / a desk)

Activity 1 — Pair Speaking (3–5 min, pairs):

methodology.title: 2.1 Core Principle: The "-ed" Sound Sorting (Phân loại âm đuôi -ed)
content: Problem: Học sinh thường phát âm sai đuôi "-ed" của động từ có quy tắc, có xu hướng đọc mọi từ là /ɪd/ (ví dụ: mix-ed, use-ed) thay vì phân biệt /t/, /d/, và /ɪd/.
Solution: Trong bối cảnh "Lớp học Mỹ thuật" (The Art Class), giáo viên nhấn mạnh đuôi "-ed" chỉ hành động đã hoàn thành trong quá khứ. Giáo viên hướng dẫn phân loại âm:
Nhóm /ɪd/ (kết thúc bằng t/d): painted, folded, started, created.
Nhóm /d/ (âm hữu thanh): colored, glued, designed, used.
Sử dụng TPR: Vỗ tay một nhịp tách biệt khi đọc nhóm /ɪd/ để học sinh nhận thức được âm tiết tăng thêm.

games.name: Vocab Slam
games.session_fit: All formats — best after vocab intro (P3) in any session
games.materials: Vocab flashcards W23: painted, colored, glued, folded, used
instructions: Round 1: Teacher calls a Vietnamese meaning — first student to say the English word AND use it correctly in a sentence wins the card.
Round 2: Reverse — teacher calls English word, student gives Vietnamese + memory trick.
Bonus round: Students chain all vocab words (painted, colored, glued, folded, used) into one connected story using sequence connectors from this week.
Team variant: 2 teams, 10 cards per round. Team with highest score wins.

games.name: Grammar Relay
games.session_fit: Best in Drill slot (Slot 2) or after P4/P6 in 3-session mode
games.materials: 10 sentence cards — 5 correct, 5 with errors based on: More regular verbs (-ed) in creative context
instructions: Grammar focus this week: More regular verbs (-ed) in creative context.
Speed Read: Display sentence for 5 sec. Teams write C (correct) or E (error) on whiteboards simultaneously — no copying allowed.
Fix-It: For error sentences, team that corrects fastest AND explains the rule earns double points.
Build: Each team member adds 1 original sentence using the grammar target. The chain must be logically connected — each sentence must link to the previous.

games.name: Story Race
games.session_fit: All formats — best in final slot of the week (S3 / Slot 5 / Session B)
games.materials: Story starter card: theme "The Art Class — The Art Room Evidence"
instructions: Give each pair a story starter connected to this week's theme: "The Art Class — The Art Room Evidence".
Pair A adds 2 sentences — must include at least 2 vocab words from this week.
Pass to Pair B: they MUST correct any grammar mistake from Pair A first, then add 2 more sentences using different vocab words.
Final round: Each pair presents their story ending aloud. Class votes on most creative + most accurate (painted, colored, glued, folded, used usage). Teacher scores grammar precision.

methodology.title: 2.1 Core Principle: The "Because" Bridge (Cây cầu "Because")
content: Problem: Students can say "I was scared," but they often struggle to develop longer sentences to explain the reason, or they use the incorrect tense in the causal clause.

Solution: Introduce the "Because Bridge" concept. This bridge connects a past Emotion to a past Reason. Structure: [Subject] + was/were + [Emotion] + BECAUSE + [Past Clause]. The teacher uses TPR (Total Physical Response): demonstrating the emotion with facial expressions or gestures (e.g., holding the stomach to feign hunger), creating a bridge shape with both hands when saying "because," and then acting out the reason (e.g., shaking the head and pointing to the mouth to show "I didn't eat").

content: The Brain and Emotions (Não bộ và Cảm xúc)

The diagram shows: Inside your brain, there is a small part called the Amygdala. It looks like an almond! The amygdala controls your feelings. When you see a big dog, your amygdala sends an alarm: "Be scared!" When you solve a mystery, it says: "Be proud!" Your brain is the boss of your emotions.

games.name: Vocab Slam
games.session_fit: All formats — best after vocab intro (P3) in any session
games.materials: Vocab flashcards W24: scared, tired, hungry, thirsty, excited
instructions: Round 1: Teacher calls a Vietnamese meaning — first student to say the English word AND use it correctly in a sentence wins the card.
Round 2: Reverse — teacher calls English word, student gives Vietnamese + memory trick.
Bonus round: Students chain all vocab words (scared, tired, hungry, thirsty, excited) into one connected story using sequence connectors from this week.
Team variant: 2 teams, 10 cards per round. Team with highest score wins.

games.name: Grammar Relay
games.session_fit: Best in Drill slot (Slot 2) or after P4/P6 in 3-session mode
games.materials: 10 sentence cards — 5 correct, 5 with errors based on: "I was [feeling] because..." (Was/Were + Adjectives)
instructions: Grammar focus this week: "I was [feeling] because..." (Was/Were + Adjectives).
Speed Read: Display sentence for 5 sec. Teams write C (correct) or E (error) on whiteboards simultaneously — no copying allowed.
Fix-It: For error sentences, team that corrects fastest AND explains the rule earns double points.
Build: Each team member adds 1 original sentence using the grammar target. The chain must be logically connected — each sentence must link to the previous.

games.name: Story Race
games.session_fit: All formats — best in final slot of the week (S3 / Slot 5 / Session B)
games.materials: Story starter card: theme "The Time Detective Agency — The Emotion Case"
instructions: Give each pair a story starter connected to this week's theme: "The Time Detective Agency — The Emotion Case".
Pair A adds 2 sentences — must include at least 2 vocab words from this week.
Pass to Pair B: they MUST correct any grammar mistake from Pair A first, then add 2 more sentences using different vocab words.
Final round: Each pair presents their story ending aloud. Class votes on most creative + most accurate (scared, tired, hungry, thirsty, excited usage). Teacher scores grammar precision.

methodology.title: 2.1 Core Principle: Problem and Solution
content: Problem: Students often list past events using "and... and... and..." without clear chronological markers, making narratives sound flat and repetitive.
Solution: Introduce the 5 core sequence adverbs (First, Next, Then, After that, Finally) as sentence starters to map out chronological narratives using regular past tense verbs.

methodology.title: 2.2 Session Flow (120 Minutes)
2.3 Vocabulary Tiering System
2.4 Teacher Notes: Pull-Out Tasks & Communicative Task
content: Pull-out oral tasks (teacher does these with 1–2 students while class works):
S1 pull-out: Show sequence flashcards. Student must link two actions orally: "First, I walked. Then, I played."
S2 pull-out: Give a 3-step prompt (wake up, eat, play). Student answers in full past tense using "First, Next, Finally."
S3 pull-out: Student reads S3 VC script. Teacher notes pronunciation errors on sequence words and recasts gently.
Communicative task (Step 5 — 10 min — MUST have real information gap):

Students piece together a 4-step story. Student A has events 1 and 3. Student B has events 2 and 4. They must ask each other "What happened [first/next]?" and write the missing steps to complete the narrative.
Materials needed: Print 2 copies of Card A and 2 copies of Card B from Section 8.
First: Hold up one index finger confidently.
Then / Next: Move hand in a small jump to the right.
After that: Make a sweeping arch motion with the hand.
Finally: Two hands push down flat, signaling the end.
Common errors to watch during pull-out:
Error: Forgetting the comma pause. "First I walked..."
Recast: "Listen: First, [pause] I walked. You try."
Error: Mixing present tense with past sequences. "Next, I play football."

games.name: Vocab Slam
games.session_fit: All formats — best after vocab intro (P3) in any session
games.materials: Vocab flashcards W25: first, then, next, after that, finally
instructions: Round 1: Teacher calls a Vietnamese meaning — first student to say the English word AND use it correctly in a sentence wins the card.
Round 2: Reverse — teacher calls English word, student gives Vietnamese + memory trick.
Bonus round: Students chain all vocab words (first, then, next, after that, finally) into one connected story using sequence connectors from this week.
Team variant: 2 teams, 10 cards per round. Team with highest score wins.

games.name: Grammar Relay
games.session_fit: Best in Drill slot (Slot 2) or after P4/P6 in 3-session mode
games.materials: 10 sentence cards — 5 correct, 5 with errors based on: Past Simple verbs + Sequence Adverbs
instructions: Grammar focus this week: Past Simple verbs + Sequence Adverbs.
Speed Read: Display sentence for 5 sec. Teams write C (correct) or E (error) on whiteboards simultaneously — no copying allowed.
Fix-It: For error sentences, team that corrects fastest AND explains the rule earns double points.
Build: Each team member adds 1 original sentence using the grammar target. The chain must be logically connected — each sentence must link to the previous.

games.name: Story Race
games.session_fit: All formats — best in final slot of the week (S3 / Slot 5 / Session B)
games.materials: Story starter card: theme "My Weekend — Routines and Sequences"
instructions: Give each pair a story starter connected to this week's theme: "My Weekend — Routines and Sequences".
Pair A adds 2 sentences — must include at least 2 vocab words from this week.
Pass to Pair B: they MUST correct any grammar mistake from Pair A first, then add 2 more sentences using different vocab words.
Final round: Each pair presents their story ending aloud. Class votes on most creative + most accurate (first, then, next, after that, finally usage). Teacher scores grammar precision.

quick_ref.Theme: Time Detective Agency — Case File: My Weekend
quick_ref.Grammar Focus: Review: Past Simple (Regular verbs & was/were) + Sequence Words
quick_ref.Vocabulary: 5 Tier 1 (production) + 3 Tier 2 (reception)

methodology.title: 2.1 Core Principle: Project-Based Review
content: Problem: Students often forget past tense structures when trying to tell a longer, connected story.

Solution: This week introduces no new grammar. Instead, it consolidates Block B learning (Past Simple, feelings, sequence words) through a hands-on project: creating a 4-panel comic strip. The visual panels anchor the chronological sequence ("First", "Then") and emotional states ("was happy").

methodology.title: 2.2 Session Flow (120 Minutes)
content: Session 1: Review past simple verbs and sequence words. Draft Panels 1 & 2 of the comic.
Session 2: Review "was/were" and emotion adjectives. Draft Panels 3 & 4.
Session 3: Finalize the comic strip and practice the oral presentation.

methodology.title: 2.3 Vocabulary Tiering System
2.4 Teacher Notes: Pull-Out Tasks & Communicative Task
content: S1 pull-out: Student picks a sequence card ("First") and a verb card ("played"), then makes a full past tense sentence.
S2 pull-out: Show an emotion flashcard. Student says "I was [feeling]" and gives one past tense reason (e.g., "I was tired. I cleaned my room.").
Communicative task (Step 5): Information Gap. Student A has Panel 1 and 3 of a mystery comic. Student B has Panel 2 and 4. They must ask questions to complete the story sequence.

parts.title: PART 6: STEM/CLIL — How to Make a Comic
content: Read this: A comic tells a story using pictures and words. It uses panels (boxes) to show time passing. The first panel shows what happened first. games.name: Vocab Slam
games.session_fit: All formats — best after vocab intro (P3) in any session
games.materials: Vocab flashcards W26: played, helped, watched, happy, tired
instructions: Round 1: Teacher calls a Vietnamese meaning — first student to say the English word AND use it correctly in a sentence wins the card.
Round 2: Reverse — teacher calls English word, student gives Vietnamese + memory trick.
Bonus round: Students chain all vocab words (played, helped, watched, happy, tired) into one connected story using sequence connectors from this week.
Team variant: 2 teams, 10 cards per round. Team with highest score wins.

games.name: Grammar Relay
games.session_fit: Best in Drill slot (Slot 2) or after P4/P6 in 3-session mode
games.materials: 10 sentence cards — 5 correct, 5 with errors based on: Review: Past Simple (Regular verbs & was/were) + Sequence Words
instructions: Grammar focus this week: Review: Past Simple (Regular verbs & was/were) + Sequence Words.
Speed Read: Display sentence for 5 sec. Teams write C (correct) or E (error) on whiteboards simultaneously — no copying allowed.
Fix-It: For error sentences, team that corrects fastest AND explains the rule earns double points.
Build: Each team member adds 1 original sentence using the grammar target. The chain must be logically connected — each sentence must link to the previous.

games.name: Story Race
games.session_fit: All formats — best in final slot of the week (S3 / Slot 5 / Session B)
games.materials: Story starter card: theme "Memories — Review & Project 2 (My Weekend Comic)"
instructions: Give each pair a story starter connected to this week's theme: "Memories — Review & Project 2 (My Weekend Comic)".
Pair A adds 2 sentences — must include at least 2 vocab words from this week.
Pass to Pair B: they MUST correct any grammar mistake from Pair A first, then add 2 more sentences using different vocab words.
Final round: Each pair presents their story ending aloud. Class votes on most creative + most accurate (played, helped, watched, happy, tired usage). Teacher scores grammar precision.

teacher_contents.stem_extension:
STEM/CLIL Extension Notes (teacher only):

PART 6: STEM/CLIL CONNECTION
How to Make a Comic
Read this: A comic tells a story using pictures and words. It uses panels (boxes) to show time passing. The first panel shows what happened first. The next panels show what happened after that. Drawing a comic helps you plan a story in your brain. You draw the action, and then you write the words!
Write 2 sentences applying the CLIL concept:
A comic uses panels to show ____________________________________________________________
First, you draw the action, and then you ____________________________________________________________
[O Bonus]: Why are panels important in a comic? ____________________________________________________________

quick_ref.Theme: Time Detective Agency — The Garden Mystery
quick_ref.Grammar Focus: Present Simple for Facts (It grows, It needs) vs. Past Simple
quick_ref.Vocabulary: 10 Tier 1 (production) + 2 Tier 2 (reception)
quick_ref.Spiral Review: W19–W26: Past Simple, Sequence words, Feelings

methodology.title: 2.1 Core Principle: Present Facts vs. Past Actions
content: Problem: Students often confuse present facts with past events when storytelling.

Solution: Introduce the Present Simple specifically for universal, scientific facts (e.g., "A seed needs water"), explicitly contrasting it with the Past Simple used for specific historical actions (e.g., "Yesterday, I planted a seed").

methodology.title: 2.2 Session Flow (120 Minutes)
content: Session 1: Introduce plant vocabulary and Present Simple for general facts.
Session 2: Contrast Present Simple facts with Past Simple narratives.
Session 3: Mastery of explaining the plant growth process.

methodology.title: 2.3 Vocabulary Tiering System
2.4 Teacher Notes: Pull-Out Tasks & Communicative Task
content: S1 pull-out: Show a plant part flashcard. Student states a fact about it (e.g., "The stem grows up.").
S2 pull-out: Ask a contrast question: "What did you do yesterday? What does a plant do every day?"
Communicative task (Step 5): Information Gap. Student A has half the facts about a sunflower, Student B has the other half. They ask questions to complete the growth chart.

parts.title: PART 1: READING INPUT  The Garden Mystery: How Plants Grow Detective Luna is investigating the garden! "How do plants grow?" she asks. The gardener explains: "First, you plant a seed in the soil. The seed is small and brown. Then, you water it. Plants need water to grow. Next, the sun shines on the soil. Plants need sunlight too. After that, roots grow down into the soil. A small stem grows up! Then, leaves appear on the stem. The plant has green leaves. Finally, a beautiful flower blooms! A plant needs three things: soil, water, and sun. That's the secret!"

games.name: Vocab Slam
games.session_fit: All formats — best after vocab intro (P3) in any session
games.materials: Vocab flashcards W27: seed, soil, water, sun, root
instructions: Round 1: Teacher calls a Vietnamese meaning — first student to say the English word AND use it correctly in a sentence wins the card.
Round 2: Reverse — teacher calls English word, student gives Vietnamese + memory trick.
Bonus round: Students chain all vocab words (seed, soil, water, sun, root) into one connected story using sequence connectors from this week.
Team variant: 2 teams, 10 cards per round. Team with highest score wins.

games.name: Grammar Relay
games.session_fit: Best in Drill slot (Slot 2) or after P4/P6 in 3-session mode
games.materials: 10 sentence cards — 5 correct, 5 with errors based on: Present Simple for Facts (It grows, It needs) vs. Past Simple
instructions: Grammar focus this week: Present Simple for Facts (It grows, It needs) vs. Past Simple.
Speed Read: Display sentence for 5 sec. Teams write C (correct) or E (error) on whiteboards simultaneously — no copying allowed.
Fix-It: For error sentences, team that corrects fastest AND explains the rule earns double points.
Build: Each team member adds 1 original sentence using the grammar target. The chain must be logically connected — each sentence must link to the previous.

games.name: Story Race
games.session_fit: All formats — best in final slot of the week (S3 / Slot 5 / Session B)
games.materials: Story starter card: theme "Memories — The Garden Mystery"
instructions: Give each pair a story starter connected to this week's theme: "Memories — The Garden Mystery".
Pair A adds 2 sentences — must include at least 2 vocab words from this week.
Pass to Pair B: they MUST correct any grammar mistake from Pair A first, then add 2 more sentences using different vocab words.
Final round: Each pair presents their story ending aloud. Class votes on most creative + most accurate (seed, soil, water, sun, root usage). Teacher scores grammar precision.

methodology.title: 2.1 Core Principle: Implicit Grammar through Storytelling
content: Problem: Students often struggle to memorize irregular verbs out of context.

Solution: Introduce irregular verbs (ran, slept, won, said, woke) naturally through a classic fable (The Tortoise and the Hare). Students learn the forms implicitly before explicitly categorizing them in the coming weeks.

methodology.title: 2.2 Session Flow (120 Minutes)
content: Session 1: Introduce the fable, key vocabulary, and preview irregular verbs.
Session 2: Focus on story sequencing, character feelings, and grammar consolidation.
Session 3: Mastery of retelling the story (Beginning, Middle, End) using past tense.

methodology.title: 2.3 Vocabulary Tiering System
2.4 Teacher Notes: Pull-Out Tasks & Communicative Task
content: S1 pull-out: Show an animal flashcard (hare/tortoise). Student states a fact: "The hare was fast."
S2 pull-out: Ask a chronological question: "What did the hare do next?"
Communicative task (Step 5): Story Circle. Students sit in pairs and take turns retelling one part of the story (Beginning, Middle, End) without looking at the text.

methodology.title: 2.5 In-Class Speaking Activity Timing (Suggested Schedule)
content: Each session has structured speaking activities that MUST be included. Full instructions are in Teacher's Contents → In-Class Speaking Activities.
① After PART 2 Vocab Building [~30 min mark]: Transport Flash-Introduction (3 min)
Pairs: Student A names a transport word, Student B gives one sentence using it.
② After PART 3 Sentence Building [~60 min mark]: Irregular Past Tense Chant (5 min)
Whole class: Teacher says base verb → students call out past form + sentence.
③ Before PART 9 Homework briefing [~110 min mark]: Speed Translation Drill (2 min)
Rapid-fire pairs: Vietnamese → English for W28 vocab.
① After PART 3 L2 Transformation [~45 min mark]: Describe & Guess transport (5 min)
Pairs: Student A describes a transport vehicle without naming it. Student B guesses.
② After PART 3 L3 Error Correction [~70 min mark]: Comparison Chains (3 min)
Class chain: Student A says 'A train is faster than a bus.' Student B continues the chain.
③ Wrap-up [~115 min mark]: Tortoise or Hare? Quick-fire (2 min)
Teacher names a transport — class calls out the character who would choose it.
① After PART 1 Reading [~25 min mark]: Round-Robin Story Chain (5 min)
Groups of 4: Each student adds one sentence to retell the Modern Race story.
② After PART 3 Sentence Building [~70 min mark]: Modern Race Debate (5 min)
Pairs: 'Which transport would you choose in the race and why?' (2-sentence answer each).
③ End of lesson [~115 min mark]: Trophy Ceremony (3 min)
Whole class votes for the pair with the best speaking this week. Winner reads their sentences.
Note: Timings are a guide. Teachers may adapt to class pace. Do NOT omit these activities — they are core to the spoken production requirement for the Cambridge Flyers Speaking standard.

parts.title: PART 1: READING INPUT  The Tortoise and the Hare
content: Once upon a time, there was a hare and a tortoise. The hare was very fast. He was proud. 'I am the fastest animal!' said the hare. The tortoise was slow, but he was patient. One day, they had a race. The hare ran very fast. Soon he was far ahead. 'I can rest,' thought the hare. He slept under a tree. But the tortoise did not stop. He walked slowly and steadily. When the hare woke up, it was too late! The tortoise crossed the finish line first. The tortoise won the race. The lesson: slow and steady wins the race.
T / F: The hare won the race.
T / F: The tortoise stopped to sleep.

What did the hare do during the race?

parts.title: PART 1: READING INPUT  The Modern Race
content: One day, the hare and the tortoise decided to have a MODERN race across the city. This time, they could each choose any type of transport. The hare was proud: 'I will ride my bicycle! I am so fast!' The tortoise was patient: 'I will take the bus. It is steady.' The race began. The hare rode his bicycle very fast. But at the traffic lights, he stopped again and again. The bus went along its steady route. It never got stuck. At every stop, the bus opened its doors, picked up passengers, and moved on. Steady. Patient. Reliable. At the finish line, the tortoise stepped off the bus first! The hare arrived later, panting. 'Not again!' he said. The lesson: being patient and choosing the right transport wins the race!

parts.title: PART 1: READING INPUT  Detective Luna's Notes: The Middle of the Race
content: Luna is writing notes about the middle of the race for her detective notebook. 'At first, the hare was far ahead. He was running fast. He looked back. The tortoise was very far behind. "I have time," thought the hare. "I will rest under this tree." The hare sat down and closed his eyes. He slept. The tortoise kept walking. Slowly. Steadily. He did not look back. He did not stop. He passed the sleeping hare. His eyes were on the finish line. Later, the hare woke up. He ran as fast as he could. But he was too late. The tortoise had already crossed the finish line.'
T / F: The hare looked back and saw the tortoise coming.
T / F: The tortoise woke the hare up.
Why did the hare decide to sleep?
What did the tortoise do when the hare was sleeping?
Fill-in from text: The tortoise passed the ____________________ hare.

parts.title: PART 6: STEM/CLIL — Transport Strategy: Speed vs Reliability
content: In real life, the FASTEST transport is not always the BEST choice:
• A motorbike (80 km/h) is faster than a bus (30 km/h) in open road.
• BUT in a city with traffic lights, a bus on a fixed route is often MORE RELIABLE.
• A bicycle (20 km/h) can use special lanes and avoid traffic jams completely.
→ This is exactly the Modern Race lesson: steady + patient = winner strategy.
→ In a city with heavy traffic, which is more reliable: motorbike or bus?
→ Which is the best transport for a short 2 km city trip? (a) ship  (b) bicycle  (c) train
→ Which real-world transport is most like the tortoise?

methodology.title: 2.1 Core Principle: Memory Tricks for Irregular Verbs
content: Problem: Học sinh thường có xu hướng thêm "-ed" vào tất cả các động từ trong quá khứ (ví dụ: go -> goed, fly -> flyed).

Solution: Tuần này giới thiệu nhóm động từ bất quy tắc đầu tiên (Nhóm Di chuyển). Giáo viên cần tập trung vào các mẹo ghi nhớ trực quan (Memory Tricks) và lặp lại liên tục thông qua kỹ thuật kể chuyện (Storytelling).

parts.title: PART 1: READING INPUT  Max's Magic Trip
content: Last summer, Max went on a magic trip! He went to the beach with his family.
They flew on a big airplane. "The airplane flew high in the sky!" said Max.
At the beach, Max ran on the sand. He ran into the cold water.
His sister came with a ball. "Come and play with me!" she said. They ran and played all day.

parts.title: PART 1: READING INPUT  Max's Magic Trip
content: Last summer, Max went on a magic trip! He went to the beach with his family.
They flew on a big airplane. "The airplane flew high in the sky!" said Max.
At the beach, Max ran on the sand. He ran into the cold water.
His sister came with a ball. "Come and play with me!" she said. They ran and played all day.
At night, a colorful bird flew across the sky. The bird came from the green forest.
Finally, they went back home. Max was tired but happy. "That was a great adventure!" he said.

Then, her family went in a fast car. They didn't fly on an airplane.

A friendly cat came to say hello. "Hello, little cat!" said Luna.

"The trip was amazing!" said Luna. "I want to go again next year."
